name: Quebec City
tagline: Old-World European Charm Without Crossing the Atlantic
description: Quebec City is the closest thing to Europe you can find in North America, with its UNESCO World Heritage Old Town, cobblestone streets, and vibrant Francophone culture. Housing costs are remarkably affordable compared to Montreal or Toronto, and universal healthcare removes one of retirement's biggest financial worries. If you speak (or want to learn) French and love history, architecture, and four-season living, Quebec City is an exceptional FIRE destination.

quickFacts.visa: No visa required for Canadian citizens. Others: Super Visa (for parents/grandparents, up to 5 years) or Visitor Record extensions. Quebec has its own immigration system — no dedicated retirement visa pathway.
quickFacts.language: French (primary); English understood in tourist areas but French is essential for daily life
quickFacts.safetyRating: Very High – one of the safest cities in North America
quickFacts.nearestAirport: Quebec City Jean Lesage International Airport (YQB)
quickFacts.climate: Humid continental with cold, snowy winters and warm, pleasant summers

housing.description: Studio or older one-bedroom in Limoilou, Saint-Sauveur, or Charlesbourg — charming older buildings

dining.description: Mostly home cooking; bistro, poutine, and boulangerie outings a couple of times a week

healthcare.description: RAMQ covers essentials; small extended-health + mandatory Quebec drug-plan premium

transportation.description: RTC monthly pass (~C$99.50); the Old Town is very walkable

entertainment.description: Free Old-Town and Plains-of-Abraham walks, Carnaval, library, community centres

1M.lifestyle: A studio or older one-bedroom in Limoilou, Saint-Sauveur, or Charlesbourg — charming older buildings at some of the lowest rents of any major Canadian city. Most meals are cooked at home, with bistro and boulangerie outings a couple of times a week, and the walkable Old Town plus an RTC pass cover getting around. RAMQ handles doctors and hospitals, leaving a small extended-health-and-drug supplement, and cheap Hydro-Québec power keeps utilities low. French is essential for daily life and winters are long and snowy — but the free Old-Town-and-Plains-of-Abraham lifestyle makes a lean budget genuinely pleasant.

housing.description: Proper one-bedroom in Saint-Jean-Baptiste or Montcalm, steps from the Old Town

dining.description: Regular bistro and brasserie dining and weekend brunch

healthcare.description: RAMQ plus private supplemental (dental, vision, physio)

transportation.description: A reliable car for Laurentian trips, winter tires, insurance

entertainment.description: Theatre, cross-country skiing, Festival d'été, museums, gym

2M.lifestyle: A proper one-bedroom in Saint-Jean-Baptiste or Montcalm, steps from the Old Town, with regular bistro dining, a car for weekend skiing in the Laurentians or trips to Île d'Orléans, and private supplemental cover. The walkable, intimate neighbourhood feel and a full cultural calendar make this a comfortable, distinctly Francophone routine with a solid margin.

housing.description: Nice or heritage one-bedroom in Old Quebec, Montcalm, or Sillery

dining.description: Frequent fine dining at rooms like Laurie Raphaël and Chez Muffy

healthcare.description: RAMQ plus comprehensive private cover for faster access

transportation.description: A late-model AWD car (Quebec SAAQ insurance is cheaper than BC's)

entertainment.description: Orchestra and theatre season tickets, Mont-Sainte-Anne / Le Massif ski passes

3M.lifestyle: A heritage one-bedroom in Old Quebec, Montcalm, or a unit in Sillery with river glimpses, with regular fine dining at rooms like Laurie Raphaël and Chez Muffy. Season tickets to the orchestra and theatre, ski passes at Mont-Sainte-Anne and Le Massif, and a good AWD car for winter round out the leisure, and comprehensive private cover layers on top of RAMQ. Quebec City is affordable enough that this tier carries a large discretionary margin.

housing.description: Luxury heritage one-bedroom or junior-two-bedroom in Old Quebec or Montcalm

dining.description: Fine dining as routine plus wine-pairing occasions

healthcare.description: RAMQ plus executive-health and premium private supplements

transportation.description: A luxury vehicle plus flights from YQB

entertainment.description: Arts patronage, private ski lessons, exclusive cultural events, spa retreats

domesticHelp.description: Weekly housekeeping plus snow removal and gardening

luxuryExtras.description: A Charlevoix cottage, quarterly European travel, art collecting

5M.lifestyle: A luxury heritage one-bedroom or junior-two-bedroom in Old Quebec or Montcalm, frequent fine dining, a nice car, and a weekly housekeeper. Arts patronage, a Charlevoix cottage for weekends, and premium private cover put this firmly into upscale European-flavoured living, well above what the local cost of living requires.

housing.description: Prime heritage-luxury apartment in Old Quebec (concierge building)

dining.description: Near-daily fine dining and catered soirées

transportation.description: Multiple luxury vehicles with a driver and chartered flights

entertainment.description: Major cultural philanthropy, private events at historic venues, extensive travel

domesticHelp.description: Full domestic help — housekeeper plus property support

luxuryExtras.description: Multiple properties, first-class travel, art patronage, a community foundation

10M.lifestyle: A prime heritage-luxury apartment in Old Quebec — a concierge building with parking, the top of a genuinely thin luxury-rental market — with near-daily fine dining and catered soirées, a luxury vehicle with a driver, chartered flights from YQB, full domestic help, and concierge-grade private cover. Quebec City is small and its high-end services are limited, so this level of spending only makes full sense alongside extensive travel or a country property in Charlevoix; much of the budget funds experiences elsewhere while enjoying 400 years of French-Canadian culture in one of North America's safest cities.
